raw_response:
I farm in Quzhou County, so I will stick with what fits my land, water, labor, and weather best. For me, the main choice is still the wheat-maize rotation, because it is the most stable system here on the North China Plain. At the start of this growing season, my winter wheat is already in the ground from last autumn, so I will manage it through harvest in early summer, then I will plant summer maize right after. I would rather keep a simple plan than spread myself too thin at my age, and this rotation lets me use the same fields, the same machinery habits, and the same timing I know well. I will use improved seed for wheat because it is steadier and easier to manage, and hybrid seed for maize because the yield is better if I can keep up with water and fertilizer. I will control fertilizer use instead of pushing too hard, because too much input costs money and can lodge the crop or waste water. I will irrigate wheat more than maize, because wheat here usually needs more help, especially around jointing and grain filling. I will use rotary tillage after harvest because it is practical and fits the way I would turn fields around quickly between crops. For pests and diseases, I will spray only as much as the crop usually needs in a normal year, with a bit more attention on wheat diseases and maize borers if pressure shows up. My goal is not the highest possible yield. My goal is a stable harvest and manageable work.
